transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-01 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (AE), Priya Singh (SE), Maya Torres (CSM) - Redwood; Dr. Samir Rao, Carla Mendes, Ethan Brooks - NexaHealth

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll kick off, do a quick round robin, then Priya will walk through the benchmark results we ran last week.
[00:18] Dr. Samir Rao: Yeah hi, Samir here. Quick heads up from our side Carla's got the infra notes, and we had one odd failure on the sample runner.
[00:30] Priya Singh: Cool, hi Samir, hey Ethan, Carla; so I pushed the first set of runs to the shared folder, link in the notes, it's the hosted run on redwood-prod with 2 models — the baseline alpaca-ish model and the tuned variant.
[00:47] Carla Mendes: Link? I didn't see it in the calendar notes.
[00:52] Maya Torres: We'll paste it in chat in a sec, sorry I forgot to attach.
[01:10] Priya Singh: Sorry for the confusion; here's the folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/nexa-poc/benchmarks (note: access is limited to recipients)
[01:25] Ethan Brooks: Got it. so general question — for the dedicated pilot are we going to run on your dedicated GPU cluster or on our VPC? we want to be clear on what the onboarding steps are.
[01:40] Jordan Lee: Good question; short answer: for the first week we'll do hosted to get baseline numbers, then we can spin up Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private in your VPC depending on the security needs. For private we need kubeconfig + service account (least privilege) and KMS access for keys.
[01:58] Dr. Samir Rao: Right, the security team will want to see SOC2 docs and the KMS flow. Do you have an HSM option?
[02:10] Priya Singh: Yes HSM/KMS integrations are supported; I can paste the security doc link after this call. We do get asked about disk encryption and audit logs — we log token-level traces only if explicitly enabled.
[02:25] Carla Mendes: We need the dev VPC creds so we can run the smoke tests; we have a strict provisioning process, so I'll try to share by tomorrow.
[02:35] Jordan Lee: Perfect — that unblocks the private deploy checks.
[02:45] Priya Singh: Back to the benchmark: the baseline model p50 was 120ms per token, p95 around 480ms on hosted. The tuned variant with 8-bit quant and our batching profile dropped p95 to 330ms but p99 spiked on longer sequences — looks like kv-cache thrash under our test workload.
[03:10] Dr. Samir Rao: When you say kv-cache thrash, do you mean the KV cache gets spilled to CPU? that was our worry with longer context.
[03:20] Priya Singh: Exactly, in our hosted infra we try to keep KV on GPU but for sequences above ~2.5k tokens some models force memory pressure and we fall back to a hybrid path; that's visible in the logs. There's a mitigation — pinned K-V cache and lower batch concurrency plus token-level caching for repeated prefixes.
[03:40] Ethan Brooks: Ok, that makes sense, tradeoff is cost vs latency. If we pin KV cache in Dedicated, does that require more GPU RAM or different instance types?
[03:52] Priya Singh: It does — pinned cache means each worker needs enough VRAM to hold full KV for pinned contexts; we can give an instance recommendation after we see your typical seq length distribution. For NEXA's case Samir said average is 900 tokens but tail to 3k for some dialogs.
[04:12] Dr. Samir Rao: Yes that's accurate — most interactions are sub-1k but the clinical note generation goes long. We can anonymize samples for tuning.
[04:24] Priya Singh: Great, please drop those samples in the drive. For the tuning plan, we'll run two passes: a quality sweep on the tuned variant with your eval set and a latency pass with our batching profiles. We'll iterate quantization settings if quality regresses.
[04:40] Jordan Lee: Quick note on billing — the hosted pilot credit will still apply; if we move to Dedicated pilot we'll issue an estimate in the SOW. I'll follow up with pricing.
[04:52] Carla Mendes: One more infra question: is there a recommended kubeconfig format? our security team clamps down on wide-scoped service accounts.
[05:02] Priya Singh: We recommend a service account scoped only to the namespace with pull secrets for the model images. We'll send a sample manifest.
[05:12] Maya Torres: I'll include it in the post-call email along with security links.
[05:20] [00:05:20] Priya Singh: Moving on, I'll walk through the concrete numbers in the sheet — opening the sheet now, so first tab is quality eval, second tab is perf logs.
[05:35] [00:05:35] Priya Singh: Quality: baseline BLEU-ish scores and human eval — the tuned variant improved relevance on 3 of 5 prompts, but hallucination on a specific prompt type increased slightly; flagged that as a regression.
[05:55] Dr. Samir Rao: Which prompt type? the ones that include patient history?
[06:03] Priya Singh: Yeah the 'multi-history synthesis' prompts. Might be due to the quantization step; we need to run a half-precision pass.
[06:12] Ethan Brooks: Is the regression reproducible locally? we might prefer to run a local eval before we invest in dedicated infra.
[06:20] Priya Singh: It is reproducible on our test harness; I can share the exact seed and harness commands.
[06:28] Carla Mendes: That'd help our infra team replicate.
[06:32] [00:06:32] Jordan Lee: Are there any blockers from compliance for the dev VPC access?
[06:38] Carla Mendes: We need the least-priv infra manifest and the SOC2 packet; once we validate we'll share credentials into a short-lived vault.
[06:46] Priya Singh: Noted. Also we captured one error in the runner: out-of-memory on model variant 'redwood-tuned-v1' when batch size > 4 for the 3k sequence test. That's the KV thrash again.
[07:00] Dr. Samir Rao: Could dynamic batching be tuned to avoid that? maybe cap batch size for long sequences and turn on adaptive batching.
[07:10] Priya Singh: Yes, adaptive batching with sequence-length bucketing helps; Redwood Optimize suggests heuristics. We'll send the recommended autoscaling and batching json.
[07:22] Ethan Brooks: I remember seeing a mention of pref-caching — can you elaborate?
[07:27] Priya Singh: Prefix caching stores common prefixes (e.g., templates) in the KV so repeated prompts are much faster; for clinical templates that helps a lot. There is a small storage overhead.
[07:40] [00:07:40] Jordan Lee: Switching gears — security review ask: Samir, what do you need from our side to start the security checklist?
[07:47] Dr. Samir Rao: SOC2 report, ISO certs if we have, encryption-at-rest details, KMS/HSM integration docs, and any pen-test summary. Also we need RBAC diagrams.
[07:58] Maya Torres: We'll attach SOC2 and the HSM integration doc; RBAC diagram we'll make a trimmed version for your team.
[08:06] Carla Mendes: Great. Also pad the SLOs we can expect in Dedicated, e.g., p95 latency targets.
[08:13] Priya Singh: For the instance class we suggested p95 ~ 200-300ms for sub-1k sequences; longer sequences will be higher. We'll provide expected ranges per instance type.
[08:25] [00:08:25] Priya Singh: Next, a quick demo of the logs — see perf_log_20271128.txt, you can see spikes aligning with p99 events; I'll highlight them.
[08:40] [00:08:40] Priya Singh: (reads) at 14:12:03 we see 'kv-fallback' triggered, memory pressure then fall back to host memcpy path, latency spike to 1.2s.
[08:52] Carla Mendes: Ok that's the exact behavior we saw.
[08:56] Dr. Samir Rao: Any quick wins to avoid that besides dedicated bigger GPUs?
[09:02] Priya Singh: Short term — cap batch size for long sequences, enable prefix caching, and increase token-interval timeout. Mid-term — move long-session workloads to dedicated hosts with pinned KV cache.
[09:14] [00:09:14] Jordan Lee: For the pilot, would you be open to a hybrid routing policy — route short chats to hosted and long-generation tasks to dedicated?
[09:23] Ethan Brooks: That actually fits our product pattern. We can start with routing rules.
[09:29] Priya Singh: We can define traffic policy based on prompt length or user bucket; Redwood Console supports per-route rules and automatic fallback.
[09:38] Dr. Samir Rao: How much work to set up the routing rules?
[09:42] Priya Singh: Minimal — a config file and a canary; we can help with the initial rule and the rollout.
[09:48] [00:09:48] Jordan Lee: On timelines — if Carla can get us dev creds by 12/2 and Priya uploads the benchmark results by 12/3 we can schedule the tuning session the week of 12/6. Does that timeline sound OK?
[10:00] Carla Mendes: Sounds reasonable.
[10:04] Dr. Samir Rao: Yes. Also we want to see a short doc on data residency for patient PII — in particular what logs get stored and for how long.
[10:14] Maya Torres: We'll include retention defaults and options to disable logging.
[10:18] Priya Singh: Quick note — in the hosted pilot logs we redacted PII by default; for Private you control retention.
[10:26] [00:10:26] Priya Singh: Any other open tech questions?
[10:29] Carla Mendes: One more: how do you handle model upgrades during a pilot? automatic or manual?
[10:35] Priya Singh: Rollouts are controlled — canary then A/B. We don't auto-upgrade model variants in a customer tenant unless you opt in. We'll capture the policy in the SOW.
[10:46] [00:10:46] Jordan Lee: Alright, quick recap of decisions: 1) Customer to share dev VPC creds and samples; 2) Priya runs latency + throughput benchmark and shares logs; 3) Redwood to send security pack + SOW + pricing; 4) Schedule tuning week of 12/6.
[11:05] Dr. Samir Rao: That captures it.
[11:10] Ethan Brooks: Thanks, team — appreciate the clarity.
[11:15] Maya Torres: I'll follow up with the email and attachments.
[11:20] Priya Singh: I'll run the benchmark and upload results by Friday.
[11:25] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the tuning pass.
[11:30] (meeting ends)

Notes / links referenced:
- Benchmarks & logs: https://drive.redwood.ai/nexa-poc/benchmarks
- Security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/nexa-poc-scan (will send post-call)
- SOW / pricing draft (to be attached by Jordan)

Transcript notes: transcription imperfect — occasional mis-heard acronyms (K-V cache transcribed as KV cash), timestamps approximate.
